title: send
description: Phone to hub, once welcomed: deliver a Draft to an agent Bucket (the `draft` Primitive's "send"). The hub answers with one `sent` carrying the same `key`. Unlike a `request`, a send changes the world, so it carries an idempotency key: the hub tries to deliver each key at most once, ever, and answers a key it has seen before with the answer it gave the first time, without trying again. The phone sends the same key again, unchanged, after a reconnect when no `sent` came, and a new key for every new "send". With `answer`, it answers the agent's question dialog instead (#80). No capability is needed: a hub that declares a `draft` command answers it.

key.description: The idempotency key, chosen by the phone and never reused: at least 128 random bits. The `sent` carries it back.

bucket.description: The Descriptor `id` of the agent Bucket the Draft is for.

text.description: The Draft, as the person heard it read back: the prompt the agent is to receive. With `answer`, the answer as the person heard it read back: the hub's record of the send, never typed.

answer.description: Present when the send answers the question dialog its Bucket's Descriptor shows (`dialog`, kind `question`; #80), instead of delivering `text` as a prompt: one choice per question, in order. The hub answers it only while that same dialog is open, and on screen, and refuses it otherwise. A hub that does not know this field sends `text` as a prompt, which herdr refuses while the agent is blocked on a dialog.

dialog.description: The `id` of the dialog it answers.

choice.description: One question's answer: the `option` picked (1 is the first), or, for a question that takes one (`other`), a free-text `text`.
